text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the language is cautious. The summary gives the key figures: 23.3% vs 2.3% expected, risk score 5.89, z 3.49, 41% of 99215s on low-complexity patients, and 1 of 20 documented 99215s below the billed level. But the headline and leaning ('too few returned records to judge', 'inconclusive') clash with the evidence. 45 of 116 claims (39%) were returned, 20 of the 27 99215 claims were documented, and 19 of those 20 supported the billed level. The statistical outlier signal is very strong. Calling the evidence inconclusive undersells it and does not explain why. Next steps are generic and ask for a targeted 99215 sample, even though 20 of 27 99215 charts are already in hand. C0285995 is cited as a low-complexity example but its documentation shows high MDM and 45 minutes, which cuts against the point it is meant to support, and the summary does not discuss that tension. The summary is accurate but needs the investigator to redo some framing.","problems":["Headline 'too few returned records' is inconsistent with 45 of 116 claims returned and 20 of 27 99215 claims documented.","Leaning 'inconclusive' is not reconciled with the extreme outlier metrics (10.3x expected, z 3.49); the summary does not explain the tension between the billing statistics and the documentation findings.","Next step requests a 'targeted sample of 99215 charts' even though most 99215 charts were already returned; it does not specify what to look for or which remaining 99215 claims lack documentation.","Example C0285995 is cited as low-complexity but the documentation supports high MDM at 45 minutes, which is not discussed; the example weakens rather than supports the point.","The 41% low-complexity figure is stated without the underlying counts (11 of 27), and the summary does not mention that no 99215 claims were on high-complexity patients.","The note-check line (problems 27%, late 7%) is not interpreted, so its relevance to the conclusion is unclear."]}
